options: Leading (left-side) spaces only
All spaces anywhere in the string, including the middle
Both leading and trailing spaces
Trailing (right-side) spaces only

options: A synonym for REPLACE
A function that removes all whitespace, including in the middle of the string
LTRIM(RTRIM(...)) — removing both leading and trailing whitespace in one call
A function exclusive to CHAR columns

questions.q: Do LTRIM, RTRIM, or TRIM affect spaces in the middle of a string?
options: Yes, all three remove every space in the string
Only TRIM affects internal spaces
Only RTRIM affects internal spaces
No — none of them touch internal whitespace, only leading/trailing
questions.explain: These functions are strictly about the edges of a string, not its interior.

questions.q: Why can a trailing space cause 'WHERE FirstName = \'John \'' to fail matching 'John'?
options: WHERE automatically trims all string literals before comparing
Trailing spaces are stripped automatically by SQL Server
Exact-match comparison treats 'John ' and 'John' as different strings, even though they look identical
This comparison would always succeed regardless of trailing spaces
questions.explain: Untrimmed whitespace is a common, invisible cause of comparisons silently failing to match expected rows.

questions.q: Which of these is a realistic real-world source of messy whitespace in data?
options: Whitespace never occurs in real databases
Copy-pasted data from spreadsheets or web forms, or data imported from external systems
Only numeric columns can contain unwanted whitespace
TRIM() itself introduces the whitespace it later has to remove
questions.explain: User input, copy-paste, and imports from other systems are common, realistic sources of stray whitespace.
